development.summary: A consonant disappeared and the vowel changed; gh stayed in the spelling.
development.note: A simplified account of the path to standard English. Dialects changed differently and at different times. Sound descriptions are reconstructions, not recordings; “neet” is a sound guide, not a required spelling stage.

changes.text: Old English niht used h for a consonant people pronounced. Middle English spellings included niȝt and night: ȝ (yogh) and gh were ways of writing that consonant.
The middle consonant was a friction sound, approximately like German ch in ich. In the path to standard English it disappeared, and the vowel lengthened to something like “neet”.
The long vowel later shifted to the “eye” sound in today’s night. This was part of the Great Vowel Shift. The written gh remained silent.
The central meaning stayed the dark part of the day. This connection mainly explains changes in sound and spelling.
